claims.text: Current EAM references do not adequately represent the liquid state of high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning model can be trained on ab initio data to predict atomic configurations in high-entropy alloys.
Training a machine-learning model on ab initio data can enhance EAM references.
The machine-learning model will learn complex atomic interactions and configurations not captured by traditional EAM references.
Learning those interactions and configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to traditional EAM references.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more accurate phase-behavior predictions for high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys at elevated temperatures near their melting points.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning model cannot be established without empirical validation.
Failure to significantly reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to traditional EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
